Calculate Parameter-Specific ESS

Source: R/calc_model_ess_parameter.R
calc_model_ess_parameter.Rd

Computes the effective sample size (ESS) of each parameter's weighted posterior mean: a function-specific, variance-ratio (delta-method) ESS of the weights, bounded above by their Kish ESS. run_MOSAIC() reports it in parameter_ess.csv and the auto-mode stopping rule reads it.

Usage

calc_model_ess_parameter(
  results,
  param_names,
  likelihood_col = "likelihood",
  weights = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

results

Data frame containing simulation results

param_names

Character vector of parameter names to analyze (required)

likelihood_col

Character name of the column containing log-likelihood values (default: "likelihood")

weights

Optional non-negative weights, one per row of results. NULL (default) uses the raw importance weights \(\exp(\ell - \max \ell)\).

verbose

Logical whether to print progress messages (default: FALSE)

...

Defunct arguments of the pre-1.3.0 grid estimate (n_bins, n_grid, method, marginal_method); a warning is given and they are ignored. Any other argument is an error.

Value

Data frame with columns:

  • parameter: Parameter name

  • type: Parameter type ('global' or 'location')

  • iso_code: ISO code for location parameters (NA for global)

  • ess_marginal: Function-specific ESS of the parameter's posterior mean

Details

For parameter \(\theta\) with normalised weights \(\tilde w_i\), posterior mean \(\tilde\mu = \sum_i \tilde w_i \theta_i\) and posterior variance \(\tilde\sigma^2 = \sum_i \tilde w_i (\theta_i - \tilde\mu)^2\), the delta-method variance of the self-normalised estimate \(\tilde\mu\) is \(\sum_i \tilde w_i^2 (\theta_i - \tilde\mu)^2\) (Owen 2013, eq. 9.9). This is a variance ratio, the definition behind Owen's \(n_e\) (eq. 9.13); it is not the weight-based \(n_e(f)\) of Owen's eq. 9.17, which uses weights proportional to \(w_i |f_i|\). The ESS is the number of independent posterior draws that would give the same precision: $$\mathrm{ESS}_\theta = \frac{\sum_i \tilde w_i (\theta_i - \tilde\mu)^2} {\sum_i \tilde w_i^2 (\theta_i - \tilde\mu)^2}.$$ It is computed directly from the weights, with no bandwidth or grid, and is bounded above by the Kish ESS of the weights, \((\sum w)^2/\sum w^2\). The bound is needed because both variances are estimated from the same weights: when one weight dominates, the unbounded ratio degenerates upward. For example, two draws weighted 0.99 and 0.01 give 50.5, and a near point mass on a 50,000-draw run gives close to \(n\). The bounded value is exactly \(n\) for uniform weights and about 1 for a point mass, and it falls as the weights concentrate. It is lower than the Kish ESS for a parameter whose heavy weights sit in its tails. When the weighted spread is zero (a point mass, or a parameter constant over the weighted draws), the Kish ESS is returned.

The weights are weights when supplied. run_MOSAIC() passes the weights of the ensemble members the posterior is built from (zero outside them), so parameter_ess.csv is a diagnostic of the written posterior (since MOSAIC 1.4.0; it gates nothing). Otherwise they are the raw importance weights \(w_i \propto \exp(\ell_i - \max \ell)\), which on production-scale likelihoods collapse to a point mass.

Until MOSAIC 1.3.0 this function returned a grid estimate (a weighted KDE or binned marginal rescaled by the number of draws). That estimate did not measure the posterior: its bandwidth came from the unweighted draws, so a point mass on a randomly chosen draw of a 50,000-draw production run scored a median of 2,518 against 2,541 for the run's own weights. It was removed, with its arguments n_bins, n_grid, method and marginal_method; passing any of them now warns and is otherwise ignored.

References

Owen AB (2013). Monte Carlo theory, methods and examples, chapter 9 (importance sampling), eqs. 9.9 and 9.13. https://artowen.su.domains/mc/

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Function-specific ESS under the raw importance weights
ess_results <- calc_model_ess_parameter(
  results = simulation_results,
  param_names = c("tau_i", "beta_j0_tot", "gamma_2")
)

# Under explicit posterior weights (e.g. the coarsened posterior)
ess_results <- calc_model_ess_parameter(
  results = simulation_results,
  param_names = c("tau_i", "beta_j0_tot", "gamma_2"),
  weights = simulation_results$weight_all
)
} # }
